newsitem.title: USA: AT&T Wireless, Comcast sign deal.
newsitem.headline: AT&T Wireless, Comcast sign deal.

text.p: AT&T Corp's AT&T Wireless Services and Comcast Cellular Communications Inc on Monday said they signed an intercarrier agreement for customers using their wireless data networks.
The agreement permits AT&T Wireless customers to access Comcast's Cellular Digital Packet Data (CDPD) networks in certain New Jersey, eastern Pennsylvania and Delaware markets.
Comcast Cellular also will be able to expand its wireless data coverage adjacent to existing areas and in other key markets served by AT&T Wireless Packet Data Service.
The companies expect to complete the interconnection of their wireless data networks in the first quarter of 1997.
Developed by a group of U.S. cellular providers including AT&T Wireless Services, CDPD allows data to be transmitted over the existing cellular network.

"This agreement will enable our customers to expand their wireless data usage to New York and other strategic markets throughout the United States," Holly Weller, Comcast Cellular general manager, Wireless Data Group, said in a statement.

AT&T Wireless Services' commercial CDPD markets covered under the agreement include Austin, Texas; Dallas/Fort Worth; Denver; Fresno, Calif.; Las Vegas; Miami/Fort Lauderdale; Minneapolis/St. Paul; Oklahoma City; Orlando, Fla.; Portland, Ore.; Sacramento, Calif.; Salt Lake City; San Antonio; Seattle; Tacoma, Wash.; Tampa, Fla.; Tulsa, Okla.; and West Palm Beach, Fla.
